ticket.title: Four CLI crates have no tests where their invocation spans live
ticket.description:
CONSTRAINT FOUND BEFORE STARTING 2026-11-08, which changes what this ticket can ask for.

The obvious test - a unit test in each CLI crate asserting that `InvocationSpan::start` produces a span - cannot work as
written. `emission_enabled()` returns false for any process running from `target/*/deps/<crate>-<hash>`, which is exactly
what a cargo test binary is. That guard exists because a test run once wrote synthetic failures into the only log the
suite is observed through (BW-33), and it is correct. The consequence is that the span wiring in `main` is invisible to
any test that runs inside the same process.

So this is not a ticket about writing four unit tests. It is a ticket about how to test out-of-process:

  * run the installed binary with a scratch suite root and a temporary sink, then read the log; the harness owns the
    environment, so the guard is not in the way;
  * or expose a way for a test to state its intent explicitly - an `InvocationSpan::start_with(sink)` that bypasses the
    policy, which already exists internally as `append_span_forced` for exactly this reason;
  * or accept that the proof is the manual live run already recorded on GB-339 for all ten tools, and use these crates
    only for the parts that are pure (subcommand derivation from argv, which is genuinely unit-testable).

The third option is honest and cheapest; the first is the one that would catch a regression, because it exercises the
real binary. Worth deciding deliberately rather than having the ticket quietly become "add a test that asserts nothing".
